env GOPROXY=off
env GOTOOLCHAIN=local

# A Go package that imports a .lgo package runs the dual-use union check
# over the imported scope. Export data lists a generic method there as
# "Type.method", and resolving that name by scope lookup made the compiler
# stop with "internal compiler error: assertion failed". The generated test
# main is such a Go importer, so every test of the package failed to build.

cd w
logos build ./...
logos test -count=1 ./box
stdout '^ok\s+example\.com/genmethod/box'
logos run ./main
stdout '^42 kept$'

# The check still walks the declarations of such a package: a union that is
# a constraint and a value type is refused when a Go importer reads it.
! logos test -count=1 ./dual
stderr 'union D is used as a type constraint and as a value type; Go cannot express both'

# A method signature is a value use too: the union below appears as a
# value only in a method parameter and result, so the check must walk
# method signatures to refuse it.
! logos test -count=1 ./dualmeth
stderr 'union D is used as a type constraint and as a value type; Go cannot express both'

# A hoisted local struct is a value use too: the union below appears as
# a value only in the field of a function-local struct, which the
# exporter publishes for inlining, so the check must scan hoisted types
# whose object dictionary carries no implicit type parameters.
! logos test -count=1 ./dualwrap
stderr 'union D is used as a type constraint and as a value type; Go cannot express both'

# A generic function body is a value use too: the union below appears as
# a value only in the field of a struct local to a generic function,
# which the importer cannot resolve, so the check must use the dual-use
# names recorded in the export facts.
! logos test -count=1 ./dualwrapgen
stderr 'union D is used as a type constraint and as a value type; Go cannot express both'

# A noinline function body exports no inline body: the union below still
# appears as a value only in a hoisted local struct field, so the import
# must stay refused through the dual-use names in the export facts.
! logos test -count=1 ./dualwrapnoinline
stderr 'union D is used as a type constraint and as a value type; Go cannot express both'

# An alias that only names a union constraint is a declaration, not a
# value use: the package below stays importable from Go.
logos test -count=1 ./dualalias

# Using the alias as a value still refuses the Go import.
! logos test -count=1 ./dualaliasval
stderr 'union D is used as a type constraint and as a value type; Go cannot express both'

# A dependency's hoisted holder approves nothing: the scan only trusts
# names owned by the imported package, and the dual-use facts still
# refuse the import instead of crashing on the generic local.
! logos test -count=1 ./dualcollide
stderr 'union D is used as a type constraint and as a value type; Go cannot express both'

# Same-named local dual-use unions share one source name: only
# package-scope unions travel in the export facts, so a LoGOs importer
# can still read the package.
logos build ./uselocal
logos test -count=1 ./uselocal

-- w/go.mod --
module example.com/genmethod

go 1.27

-- w/box/box.lgo --
package box

type Box struct {
	N int
}

func (b *Box) pick[T any](v T) T {
	return v
}

func (b *Box) Twice() int {
	return b.pick[int](b.N) * 2
}

func (b Box) Label[T any](v T) T {
	return v
}

-- w/box/box_test.lgo --
package box_test

import (
	"testing"

	"example.com/genmethod/box"
)

func TestTwice(t *testing.T) {
	b := &box.Box{N: 21}
	if got := b.Twice(); got != 42 {
		t.Fatalf("Twice = %d", got)
	}
}

-- w/main/main.lgo --
package main

import (
	"fmt"

	"example.com/genmethod/box"
)

func main() {
	b := &box.Box{N: 21}
	fmt.Println(b.Twice(), box.Box{}.Label[string]("kept"))
}

-- w/dual/dual.lgo --
package dual

type A struct {
	X int
}

func (a A) M() string {
	return "A"
}

func (a A) Same[T any](v T) T {
	return v
}

type B struct {
	Y string
}

func (b B) M() string {
	return "B"
}

type D interface {
	A | B
	M() string
}

func First[T D](x T) T {
	return x
}

var U D = A{X: 3}

-- w/dual/dual_test.lgo --
package dual_test

import (
	"testing"

	"example.com/genmethod/dual"
)

func TestFirst(t *testing.T) {
	if dual.First(dual.B{Y: "z"}).M() != "B" {
		t.Fatal("First")
	}
}

-- w/dualmeth/dualmeth.lgo --
package dualmeth

type A struct {
	X int
}

func (a A) M() string {
	return "A"
}

func (a A) Keep(v D) D {
	return v
}

type B struct {
	Y string
}

func (b B) M() string {
	return "B"
}

type D interface {
	A | B
	M() string
}

func First[T D](x T) T {
	return x
}

-- w/dualmeth/dualmeth_test.lgo --
package dualmeth_test

import (
	"testing"

	"example.com/genmethod/dualmeth"
)

func TestFirst(t *testing.T) {
	if dualmeth.First(dualmeth.B{Y: "z"}).M() != "B" {
		t.Fatal("First")
	}
}

func TestKeep(t *testing.T) {
	a := dualmeth.A{X: 1}
	if a.Keep(dualmeth.B{Y: "z"}).M() != "B" {
		t.Fatal("Keep")
	}
}

-- w/dualwrap/dualwrap.lgo --
package dualwrap

type A struct {
	X int
}

func (a A) M() string {
	return "A"
}

type B struct {
	Y string
}

func (b B) M() string {
	return "B"
}

type D interface {
	A | B
	M() string
}

func First[T D](x T) T {
	return x
}

func Wrap() any {
	type holder struct {
		Value D
	}
	return holder{Value: A{X: 3}}
}

-- w/dualwrap/dualwrap_test.lgo --
package dualwrap_test

import (
	"testing"

	"example.com/genmethod/dualwrap"
)

func TestFirst(t *testing.T) {
	if dualwrap.First(dualwrap.B{Y: "z"}).M() != "B" {
		t.Fatal("First")
	}
}

func TestWrap(t *testing.T) {
	if dualwrap.Wrap() == nil {
		t.Fatal("Wrap")
	}
}

-- w/dualwrapgen/dualwrapgen.lgo --
package dualwrapgen

type A struct {
	X int
}

func (a A) M() string {
	return "A"
}

type B struct {
	Y string
}

func (b B) M() string {
	return "B"
}

type D interface {
	A | B
	M() string
}

func First[T D](x T) T {
	return x
}

func Wrap[T any](v T) any {
	type holder struct {
		Value D
	}
	return holder{Value: A{X: 3}}
}

-- w/dualwrapgen/dualwrapgen_test.lgo --

	"example.com/genmethod/dualwrapgen"

		t.Fatal("First")
	}

func TestWrap(t *testing.T) {

		t.Fatal("Wrap")
	}
}

	Y string

	M() string

		Value D
	}

-- w/depwrap/depwrap.lgo --
package depwrap

func Wrap() any {
	type holder struct {
		V int
	}
	return holder{V: 1}
}

-- w/dualcollide/dualcollide.lgo --
package dualcollide

import (
	"example.com/genmethod/depwrap"
)

type A struct {
	X int
}

func (a A) M() string {
	return "A"
}

type B struct {
	Y string
}

func (b B) M() string {
	return "B"
}

type D interface {
	A | B
	M() string
}

func First[T D](x T) T {
	return x
}

func UseDep() any {
	return depwrap.Wrap()
}

func Wrap[T any](v T) any {
	type holder struct {
		Value D
	}
	return holder{Value: A{X: 3}}
}

-- w/dualcollide/dualcollide_test.lgo --
package dualcollide_test

import (
	"testing"

	"example.com/genmethod/dualcollide"
)

func TestFirst(t *testing.T) {
	if dualcollide.First(dualcollide.B{Y: "z"}).M() != "B" {
		t.Fatal("First")
	}
}

func TestUseDep(t *testing.T) {
	if dualcollide.UseDep() == nil {
		t.Fatal("UseDep")
	}
}

func TestWrap(t *testing.T) {
	if dualcollide.Wrap[int](1) == nil {
		t.Fatal("Wrap")
	}
}

-- w/duallocal/duallocal.lgo --
package duallocal

func F() int {
	type choice interface {
		int | string
	}
	type box[C choice] struct {
		v C
	}
	var c choice = 1
	return c.(int) + box[int]{v: 2}.v
}

func G() int {
	type choice interface {
		int | string
	}
	type box[C choice] struct {
		v C
	}
	var c choice = 5
	return c.(int) + box[int]{v: 4}.v
}

-- w/uselocal/uselocal.lgo --
package uselocal

import (
	"example.com/genmethod/duallocal"
)

func Total() int {
	return duallocal.F() + duallocal.G()
}

-- w/uselocal/uselocal_test.lgo --
package uselocal_test

import (
	"testing"

	"example.com/genmethod/uselocal"
)

func TestTotal(t *testing.T) {
	if uselocal.Total() != 12 {
		t.Fatalf("Total = %d", uselocal.Total())
	}
}
